paper.title: Minority opinion spreading in random geometry (Galam majority-rule model)

headline: Galam majority rule (agent-based): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; g=3 tipping at p_c=0.5 (Galam 0.5); g=4 ties->up tipping at p_c=0.24 < 0.5 (minority spreading; Galam ~0.23)

verdicts.gate: P1 g=3 majority rule: consensus + initial majority wins (tipping at 0.5)
P2 g=4 (ties->up): up-tipping point p_c < 0.5 (minority spreading)
P3 no interior stable fixed point (every trajectory flows to 0 or 1)

evidence.note: non-monotone runs are knife-edge wobble ON the unstable fixed point p_c; they still flow away to 0/1

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the Galam tipping point + minority-spreading result and would catch an artifact

citations: Galam, S. (2002). Minority opinion spreading in random geometry. Eur. Phys. J. B 25:403-406. doi:10.1140/epjb/e20020045.
Galam, S. (2008). Sociophysics: A review of Galam models. Int. J. Mod. Phys. C 19(3):409-440. doi:10.1142/S0129183108012297.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction
